text: Why must BigDecimal be constructed from a string rather than a double?
choices: A double literal has already lost the exact decimal value before BigDecimal sees it
Doubles are always negative in BigDecimal
explanation: new BigDecimal(0.10) gives 0.1000000000000000055511151231257827021181583404541015625, because the damage happened at the literal. new BigDecimal("0.10") parses the decimal text exactly and never passes through binary floating point at all. No care inside BigDecimal could repair the first case.
